messages.content: The response must contain between 77 and 99 words. Patient says their neck feels stiff and swollen around throat area and throat feels sore. As a doctor, you can see no signs of swelling, and it's confirmed not to be a respiratory infection. What are the possible causes from the data you can gather?

message.content: Based on your symptoms of stiffness, perceived swelling, and soreness without visible physical changes or respiratory infection, several non-infectious causes are likely. Musculoskeletal strain from poor posture or tension headaches often mimics throat issues. Acid reflux (GERD) can cause laryngopharyngeal reflux, leading to a sensation of fullness and pain. Allergies might trigger mild inflammation without obvious external signs. Anxiety or psychosomatic responses can also create these sensations. Dental problems like an impacted wisdom tooth may refer pain to the neck. Thyroid issues, such as hypothyroidism, rarely present with acute swelling but can cause muscle tightness. Finally, early-stage lymph node reactions to minor, undetected irritants could contribute. A thorough clinical history and targeted exams are needed to differentiate these possibilities accurately.
